title: Tenant-aware alert suppression and incident tagging for analytics pipeline
creator: Sasha Nguyen
description:
Background: As our per-tenant usage grows, the analytics ingest pipeline is generating noisy alerts from a small number of tenants during spikes (large batch uploads, synthetic traffic). These alerts are drowning out signals for multi-tenant regressions and increasing alert fatigue on oncall. We need a solution that suppresses tenant-local noise without hiding platform-level regressions, and that automatically annotates incidents with tenant metadata so triage is faster.

Goal: Implement tenant-aware alert suppression rules and incident tagging across the analytics ingestion and processing services. Deliverables: (1) a suppression policy engine that can mute alerts for tenants meeting configured criteria for a bounded window, (2) automatic enrichment of PagerDuty incidents and internal incident tickets with tenant context (tenant_id, plan, region, recent deploy id), and (3) dashboards and runbook updates to reflect suppression state and suppressed counts.

Non-goals: We are not changing SLOs in this ticket, not removing any existing SLIs, and not implementing tenant billing-based throttling here. That will be handled by a separate DDoS/usage control initiative.
acceptance_criteria: Suppression engine can be configured per-alert with: threshold window, suppression duration, reason tags, and tenant allowlist/denylist
When suppression triggers for a tenant, alert noise is suppressed for that alert key but a suppressed event is recorded to metrics and dashboard
PagerDuty incidents created from suppressed alerts include tenant metadata and a suppression flag in the summary/body
Oncall dashboard shows suppressed_alert_count, suppressed_by_tenant top-k, and suppression_rate over time
Runbook documents updated with steps to lift suppression, re-enable noisy tenant alerts, and escalate to Product when repeated
No platform-wide SLO regressions are missed during suppression — verified by synthetic probes and retrospective sampling of traces during a suppression window
tasks: Design suppression policy schema and API (backend + config store) - API design PR (confluence link below)
Implement suppression evaluation middleware in analytics-ingest and aggregator services
Emit suppressed_alert metric (tagged by alert_name, tenant_id, region) and ensure it flows to metrics pipeline
Annotate outgoing PagerDuty/ops alerts with tenant metadata and suppression flag
Add suppression panels to existing analytics observability dashboards
Update oncall runbooks and postmortem templates to include suppression context
Rollout: feature flag, canary on non-critical region, evaluate for 2 weeks, then global
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Decided suppression should be per-alert key + tenant rather than per-tenant global mute to avoid hiding cross-tenant regressions (decision by SRE/Analytics leads)
2025-02-20: Chose to record suppressed events to metrics with low-cardinality and high-cardinality views to balance cost and troubleshooting needs
2025-02-25: Will use existing config-store service (kv-config) and expose suppression controls via Console later; initial rollout will use feature flags and a YAML config file
comments: 2025-02-16 - Sasha Nguyen: Spiked with sample code to annotate alerts with tenant_id. Found that current alert keys do not always include tenant context; that's the upstream change we need.

2025-02-19 - Amir Patel: Implemented prototype middleware in analytics-ingest that injects tenant metadata from request headers and headers->alertkey mapping. POC PR: github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-ingest/pull/312

2025-02-22 - Priya Rao (SRE): Observability note - emitting suppressed_alert_count with high-cardinality tenant_id will increase metric cardinality. We'll emit low-cardinality aggregated metrics (suppressed_total_by_alert) and a sampled high-cardinality stream (1:1000) for debugging.
2025-02-28 - Product (Diego Martin): Need UI controls to manually lift suppression for a tenant; product will track follow-up work. Marking as dependency for Console feature work.

2025-03-01 - Amir Patel: Began adding PagerDuty annotation logic. PD incident body includes tenant_id, plan, region, suppression_reason and link to tenant dashboard. Waiting on PD schema approval from oncall.
2025-03-02 - Sasha Nguyen: Created initial dashboard panels in Grafana under /d/analytics/suppression-overview; panels show suppressed_rate and top 10 noisy tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (flagged): Merge suppression middleware behind feature flag; emit suppressed metrics only
Phase 1 (canary): Enable for internal staging tenants in us-west-2 for 48 hours, monitor synthetic ingestion probes and suppressed metrics
Phase 2 (limited): Enable for customers on dev-tier who opt-in, run for two weeks alongside manual reviews
Phase 3 (global): Enable by default for high-noise alert keys with automated suppression; product to add Console UI for manual overrides
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Suppression might hide true platform regressions if alert keys are too coarse. Mitigation: require at least one platform-level alert per signal that cannot be suppressed, and publish synthetic probes to validate end-to-end flow.
Risk: Metrics cardinality blowup. Mitigation: aggregate metrics at low-cardinality and stream sampled high-cardinality telemetry to a separate debug pipeline.
Risk: PagerDuty noise reduction may change oncall behavior. Mitigation: update runbooks, provide retrospective training, and allow oncall to disable suppression per-incident
